subject: Security exhibit + audit evidence cadence for Veridian Health (MSA/Order Form)
messages:
From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@veridianhealth.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@veridianhealth.com
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Security exhibit / audit rights questions for MSA + Order Form

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for the quick turnaround last week on the redlines tracker. Before we move the order form into signature, legal has a couple of asks on the security exhibit and audit language we need clarified so our compliance team can sign off:

- Can you confirm whether you will provide a SOC 2 Type II report or just Type I?
- For penetration testing, we need to understand the window (annual vs. on-demand) and whether your team will coordinate a joint test or if Veridian can run an independent test and produce a report.
- Audit rights: our auditors typically request up to 3 business days on-site or remote access for inspection. Are you able to support this, and what are the data/PII redaction boundaries?
- Evidence cadence: we have quarterly evidence requests in our procurement playbook — can you provide a sample cadence and what artifacts you can commit to delivering (logs, config snapshots, SOC report, pen-test summary, remediation timelines)?

If helpful, we can set a short call with our security manager next week. We are aiming to complete contractual signoff by 11/20 so we can onboard before year-end.

Thanks,
Sarah Nguyen
Head of Compliance
Veridian Health

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit / audit rights questions for MSA + Order Form

Sarah —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick summary and a proposed path forward below. Attaching a draft security exhibit and an audit evidence checklist to make the asks concrete.

Short answers (high level):
- SOC 2: We currently provide a SOC 2 Type II report (rolling 12-month period). We'll include the attestation under the security exhibit and a statement about availability on request.
- Pen test: Redwood runs an annual third-party penetration test and can share the summary report and remediation summary. For customer-initiated tests, we allow external tests with a technical and legal coordination window (see attachment).
- Audit rights: We typically offer scoped audit rights for SOC 2-related controls and do not provide unfettered production access. We can support remote inspection and evidence exchange; on-site visits are accommodated with 30 days notice and a limited scope.
- Evidence cadence: Proposed cadence in the attached checklist: SOC 2 report (on request, annually), quarterly evidence pack (logs sampling, config snapshots, summary of security updates), and ad-hoc remediation artifacts within SLA.

Proposed next steps:
1) Marissa (Legal) to review the draft security exhibit and send any contract redlines.
2) Karthik (Security) to confirm the technical boundaries for evidence exchange and the pen-test coordination playbook.
3) Sarah, if that works, we can lock a 30‑minute sync next Tue (11/10) to finalize scope and timeline.

Attachments: security-exhibit-draft_v1.pdf; audit-evidence-checklist.xlsx

Best,
Jordan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.ai, Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Security exhibit / audit rights questions for MSA + Order Form

Thanks for looping me in — Jordan, Sarah, I reviewed the attached exhibit and have a few contract-level redlines and rationale so we can avoid open-ended obligations that could impact other customers or security posture. High-level summary: 

1) Audit scope narrowness — We should limit audit rights to controls that are relevant to the contracted service (SOC 2 scope) and require that all audits be conducted by mutually agreeable third parties or via a vendor-provided evidence package. We should decline requests for broad network/host-level access to production.

2) On-site access / notice — Accepting a 30-day notice for on-site inspections is reasonable if we add limits: inspections only for evidence review (not hands-on access), limited to a 1-business-day window, and subject to Redwood escort and access controls.

3) Penetration testing — We will provide the annual third-party pen-test summary and remediation report. For customer-initiated tests, require a test plan, scope approval from Redwood Security, and a 45-day scheduling window to avoid conflicts with internal testing and change freezes. Also include a clause preventing destructive testing and PII exfiltration.

4) Evidence production cadence — Offer a quarterly evidence bundle (sampled logs, configuration snapshots, SOC 2 attestation) and an ad-hoc request process with reasonable limits (max 4 ad-hoc requests per year, and each request should be responded to within 10 business days).

5) Data handling / redactions — Add explicit redaction obligations and a commitment to redact customer and third-party PII from any shared artifacts. Include a standard non-disclosure language for auditors.

I attached a marked-up MSA exhibit (redlines_msa_marked.docx) with suggested language. Jordan — please confirm the timelines above with Karthik and Sarah, please confirm whether 11/10 at 10am PT works for a short call to walk through redlines.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, jordan.blake@redwood.ai, Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@veridianhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 09:37:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Security exhibit / audit rights questions for MSA + Order Form

Adding the security operations perspective and concrete constraints: 

- Live production access: Not permitted. We can provide time-bound, scoped access to redacted logs hosted in a secure, read-only share (S3 with presigned links or a secure SharePoint). Full host-level or console access is not possible.
- Logs and artifacts: We can provide sampled logs (authentication, audit trail, error logs) for the requested time range. For large data sets we will provide sampling guidance to keep the bundles manageable.
- Pen test coordination: Our standard ops playbook requires a test plan submission 45 days in advance, no destructive techniques, and a mutually agreed blast radius. We will also provide a post-test remediation plan within 15 business days. See attached pen-test-ops-playbook.pdf for details.
- Evidence cadence: Technical delivery as Marissa suggested: quarterly packages, plus up to four ad-hoc packages/year. Where external auditors need more detail, we prefer delivering redacted artifacts rather than direct interactive sessions.

Jordan — I can join the 11/10 sync and walk through the playbook and sample evidence. Sarah — please confirm whether remote sampling will satisfy Veridian's auditor; if not, point me to the specific artifacts your auditor requires.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Security Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@veridianhealth.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, procurement@veridianhealth.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit / audit rights questions for MSA + Order Form

Jordan / Marissa / Karthik —

Thanks for the thorough responses and the marked redlines — that all looks reasonable. A couple of small asks to land the scope:

- We can accept remote, redacted evidence via secure share for our auditors.
- Please add the 30-day notice for any on-site inspection to the exhibit (as Marissa suggested) and confirm the 1-business-day cap.
- For customer-initiated pen-tests, 45-day scheduling is OK, but can you confirm that Veridian will get a consolidated remediation summary (not just a pass/fail) within 15 business days post-test?

If you confirm those items in writing, Procurement will move the Order Form to signature today and I will route the MSA redlines to Legal for final review. We can skip the sync if everything above is confirmed — but I appreciate the offer.

Best regards,
Sarah Nguyen
Head of Compliance
Veridian Health
